description: The Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on NOAA-20 (JPSS-1, J1): 22 bands (M1-M16 with M16A/M16B, I1-I5, Day/Night Band low- and mid-gain stages) from 0.41 to 12.5 um. The curves are the VIIRS Data Analysis Working Group (DAWG) at-launch band-averaged relative spectral responses, V2.1 (Nov 2016; README dated 2017-10-03), the 'Final prelaunch version' published by NOAA NCC, used to populate the VIIRS SDR look-up tables.
facility_description: The Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) is NOAA's series of polar-orbiting weather satellites (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20/J1, NOAA-21/J2, ...); VIIRS is its visible/infrared imager.

notes: V2.1 changes only M9 ('to correct and update the spectral position of the M9 RSR', ~0.7 nm shorter in-band); M8, M10-M12, M14-M16(A,B), I3-I5 and DNBMGS are the V1 RSR 'repeated in V2' (README). Calibration reference: Oudrari et al. 2016, cited by NOAA's NOAA-20 performance table. Curves are the DAWG band-average files; README quotes: 'The RSR are stitched IB+OOB RSR with all RSR normalized at the peak of 1.0' and low-quality response 'is set to 1E-10 in the band average RSR'. Some V1-derived file headers label the wavelength column 'wvl_um' although the values are nm (verified: each band's peak lies inside its NOAA specification spectral range). 'RSR are provided for M16A, M16B and an average of M16A and M16B referred to as M16 ... VIIRS on-orbit M16 SDR radiances consist of a time delay integration of M16A and M16B observations' (README). DNBLGS/DNBMGS are the Day/Night Band low- and mid-gain stages. Photon/energy weighting is not stated by the owner; the staged DetectorType=energy is tagged 'assumed'. Pivot check: NOAA publishes spectral ranges, not central wavelengths (NOAA-20 VIIRS On-orbit Performance table, https://ncc.nesdis.noaa.gov/NOAA-20/docs/NOAA-20-VIIRS-on-OrbitPerformanceTable.pdf); every M/I band pivot lies inside its range. Facility/instrument IDs follow SVO's JPSS/VIIRS-J1 and JPSS/VIIRS-J2 (no SVO record was available locally to confirm the mapping; the J1/J2 suffixes are NOAA's own flight designations). Instrument paper cited is the Suomi NPP VIIRS on-orbit performance paper (same instrument design). DetectorTypeSource changed from assumed to original (2026-10-26, header only, curves unchanged): NOAA's VIIRS Radiometric Calibration ATBD (474-00027 Rev. E, effective 2022-07-22, https://www.star.nesdis.noaa.gov/jpss/documents/ATBD/D0001-M01-S01-003_JPSS_ATBD_VIIRS-SDR_E.pdf, §2.3 General Radiometric Equations, Eq. 9) states 'The Relative Spectral Response (RSR) is defined as the normalized product of the quantum efficiency, wavelength, and optical transmittance. It is normalized by the maximum value of this product.', and band-averages radiance as ∫RSR(λ)·L(λ)dλ / ∫RSR(λ)dλ (Eq. 12, 14). The wavelength factor is folded into the RSR, so it integrates directly over F_λ: energy in SED_Tools' convention (as for 2MASS).
